# Daily AI Newsletter Digest - 20/3/2026

## 🔥 Top Stories
- Google introduces "Stitch", a new AI-native design platform with an infinite canvas, voice controls, and a built-in design agent, aiming to revolutionize the design process.
- OpenAI signs a deal with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to make its AI products available to the U.S. government for both classified and unclassified work.
- Microsoft considers legal action against Amazon and OpenAI over a $50B cloud deal, citing a potential violation of their agreement.

## 🤖 AI Models & Research
- MiniMax launches M2.7, a self-evolving AI model that rivals top models like OpenAI and Anthropic on coding benchmarks, demonstrating significant advancements in AI technology.
- Anthropic publishes a qualitative AI study involving 81,000 Claude users across 159 countries, highlighting hopes and fears about AI.
- Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro is a 1-trillion-parameter foundation model with performance approaching that of models from OpenAI and Anthropic at a fraction of the cost.
- DeepMind builds a scorecard for AGI, breaking it down into 10 measurable cognitive abilities.

## 🛠️ Tools & Products
- Blink Claw is a managed platform that makes it easy to deploy OpenClaw agents, removing common barriers to using AI.
- Ollama launches MiniMax-M2.7, a new model that supports complex workflows in software engineering, office productivity, and research environments.
- Accio is a sourcing agent that helps entrepreneurs find and produce products.
- OpenAI releases smaller models designed to bring GPT-5.4's power to latency-sensitive workloads.
- Anthropic introduces Dispatch, a new research preview within Claude Cowork, allowing for persistent conversations on desktops.

## 📰 Industry News
- Meta plans to cut up to 20% of its workforce, approximately 16,000 jobs, to offset massive AI infrastructure spending.
- Elf Labs signs a major motion picture deal for wide theatrical release in China, a market worth $2 trillion.
- BuzzFeed launches a new AI spin-off called Branch Office, focused on AI apps built around creativity and social connection.
- Microsoft reorganizes its Copilot teams to unify the consumer and business experiences.

## 📚 Resources & Learning
- A step-by-step guide to generating an actionable SEO audit using AI is available.
- The Machine Payments Protocol is a new protocol that enables machine-to-machine payments.
- NASA's X-43 jet, which reached speeds of 11,854 km/h, is an example of innovative technology that has contributed to advancements in various fields.

Emerging trends:
- The increasing use of AI in various industries, including real estate, design, and healthcare.
- The development of new AI models and tools, such as MiniMax-M2.7 and Blink Claw, that support complex workflows and remove barriers to using AI.
- The growing importance of AI in government and military applications, with OpenAI's deal with AWS and the development of AI-powered systems for autonomous vehicles.
- The focus on making AI more accessible and user-friendly, with the launch of platforms like Stitch and Accio that aim to simplify the design and product development process.

## Google AI Studio Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Google AI Studio is introducing updates to its Usage Tiers and billing account tier caps for the Gemini API, starting April 1, 2026.
- Users need to review their current usage to plan ahead and prevent service disruption when the new caps take effect.
- Automated Usage Tier upgrades will be implemented, and each tier will enforce a maximum monthly spend limit at the billing account level.
- Project Spend Caps can be configured to pause requests for a specific project if the defined target is exceeded.

### Detailed Points
- Starting March 16, 2026, users can configure optional project-level spend limits, known as Project Spend Caps. If a project exceeds the defined target, the system will pause requests for that project within approximately 10 minutes. Users are responsible for any overages incurred during this brief window.
- Starting April 1, 2026, each Usage Tier will enforce a maximum monthly spend limit at the billing account level. If the aggregate spend reaches this cap, Gemini API requests tied to that billing account will be paused until the next month.
- Automated Usage Tier upgrades will be implemented, where accounts will systematically graduate to higher tiers with higher rate limits as they meet specified spend and tenure thresholds.
- Users need to manually verify and review their current usage to plan ahead and prevent service disruption. This includes checking the current Usage Tier, applicable limits, and historical monthly spending.
- If a billing account requires a higher cap, users can request an override by filling out a form.
- The Gemini API Team recommends checking the product documentation or visiting the Gemini AI community for any questions or help.

## World of AI Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Google has released Stitch 2.0, a significant update to its AI-native design platform, featuring an infinite canvas, voice controls, and a built-in design agent.
- Stitch 2.0 aims to streamline the design process, allowing for concept, design, build, and shipment of a full product without needing to open a second app.
- Anthropic has published a qualitative AI study involving 81,000 Claude users across 159 countries, highlighting hopes and fears about AI.
- The study reveals that people with the least are hoping the most from AI, and lower-income countries are more optimistic about AI's potential.

### Detailed Points
- Google's Stitch 2.0 includes features such as:
  - Infinite canvas for dropping in images, text, and code as context.
  - A design agent that reasons across the entire project and works on multiple ideas simultaneously.
  - Voice mode where users can talk to the canvas, and it makes changes in real-time.
  - Instant prototyping by stitching screens together and hitting Play to preview interactive app flows.
  - DESIGN.md, a new agent-friendly markdown file for exporting and importing design rules across tools.
- The update aims to kill the traditional design workflow, which involves multiple translation layers and losses in the process.
- Stitch 2.0 is free and available for anyone 18 and older, wherever Gemini is available.
- Anthropic's study findings include:
  - Hope and fear are not two separate camps; they coexist within the same person.
  - Independent workers are seeing real financial gains at 3x the rate of traditional employees due to AI.
  - The people most exposed to AI disruption are older, female, more educated, and higher-paid.
- The study also highlights that no country dipped below 60% positive sentiment towards AI, but lower-income countries were the most optimistic.
- Google's goal is to connect Stitch with its other tools, such as Antigravity for AI-native coding and Gemini in Chrome for browser agents, to create a seamless experience from concept to deployment.

- The new MiniMax-M2.7 model is now available to run via Ollama's cloud, designed to excel at completing end-to-end tasks in software engineering and office productivity.
- MiniMax-M2.7 features self-improvement capabilities using web data, enabling assistants like OpenClaw to perform research and learn new skills.
- Ollama now supports launching non-interactive agents using the new --yes flag, allowing for background operations on servers, scripts, and other environments.

### Detailed Points
- **MiniMax-M2.7 Model**: This new model is designed to improve character and emotional intelligence while excelling in software engineering and office productivity tasks. It utilizes web data for self-improvement, allowing it to learn and adapt over time.
- **OpenClaw Integration**: OpenClaw can now leverage MiniMax-M2.7 to perform deep research tasks and learn from up-to-date web information. This enables OpenClaw to teach itself new skills and best practices, such as financial reporting.

- **Launch Agents in Non-Interactive Mode**: Ollama's new --yes flag enables launching non-interactive agents, including OpenClaw, in the background without interruption. This is useful for servers, scripts, and other environments that do not support the OpenClaw gateway.

## TLDR Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Amazon's contract renewal negotiations with the US Postal Service have fallen apart, with Amazon planning to reduce the number of packages sent through the Postal Service.
- Google has introduced "Stitch", a vibe design tool with an AI-native canvas that can hold and reason across images, code, and text simultaneously.
- OpenAI Codex is a coding agent that can write features, fix bugs, answer questions about codebases, and propose pull requests.
- Meta will pay Instagram, TikTok, and YouTube creators with big followings to post on Facebook.
- TLDR is hiring a Senior Software Engineer, Applied AI, with a salary range of $250k-$350k, and is fully remote.

### Detailed Points
- Amazon last year committed to spending roughly $4 billion by the end of 2026 to triple the size of its rural delivery network, but now plans to sharply reduce the number of packages it sends through the Postal Service when the contract expires at the end of September.
- Stitch is a design agent that understands users' entire canvas context, allowing them to swap images, generate product briefs, or mix mobile and desktop screens on the same canvas, and can create instant prototypes to preview interactive app flow.
- OpenAI Codex has three layers: the agent loop, prompt and context management, and the multisurface architecture that lets one agent serve many different interfaces, and can run tasks in parallel while monitoring progress in real-time.
- Meta's new Creator Fast Track program offers creators guaranteed monthly payments and increased reach on Facebook, in an effort to attract popular creators from other platforms.
- Reddit's CISO and Head of Corporate Engineering, Sean Joerg, shared the playbook his team used to unify work and build an AI-ready foundation, including leading change management, gaining cross-functional buy-in, and setting up guardrails to safely unlock AI and automation.
- TransAstra, a Los Angeles-based company, plans to fly out to a smallish, near-Earth asteroid, throw a large bag around it, and bring the body back to a safe gathering point near Earth, with a feasibility study to be completed by May.
- Starlink is a true technological leap over every other form of airline Wi-Fi, with global coverage and lower orbit, but also has limitations due to the laws of physics.
- The Machine Payments Protocol is an open protocol for machine-to-machine payments, allowing developers to charge for API requests, tool calls, or content.

## JournalClub.io Newsletter

### Key Highlights
- Researchers from South China Agricultural University, led by Li et al., have developed a dynamic neural-model-based predictive control framework for autonomous wheel-legged robot systems.
- The framework incorporates a full dynamic model of the robot, rather than a simple kinematic approximation, to improve trajectory tracking and navigation in complex environments.
- The system uses a neural approximator to estimate unknown disturbances from the environment and a recurrent neural network to efficiently solve the predictive control optimization problem.

### Detailed Points
- The newsletter discusses the challenges faced by autonomous delivery robots in navigating through uneven sidewalks, construction zones, and other obstacles in urban environments.
- The authors propose a new framework for vehicle trajectory tracking that incorporates a full dynamic model of the robot, including forces, mass, inertia, friction, and physical interactions with the environment.
- The dynamic model is derived from the robot's physical dimensions, wheel arrangement, and steering geometry, and is used to predict the robot's motion and optimize control inputs.
- The framework uses a linear tire approximation to model the forces generated by each wheel, and a linearization technique to approximate the nonlinear dynamic equations at each control step.
- The system employs a model predictive control (MPC) strategy, which simulates the future and determines the optimal sequence of actions to minimize a cost function that balances trajectory tracking and control input smoothness.
- The MPC optimization problem is solved using a recurrent neural network, which allows for fast and efficient computation of the optimal control inputs.
- The system also includes a dynamic approximator that learns to estimate unknown disturbances from the environment and compensates for them in real-time.
- The approximator uses a set of fuzzy basis functions to estimate the disturbance and updates its weights continuously as the robot moves.
- The framework is designed for a six-wheel legged robot, but its lessons are broadly applicable to other autonomous vehicles and robots.

- MiniMax's M2.7 model is now publicly available via the MiniMax Agent and the MiniMax API Platform.

- Xiaomi's MiMo-V2-Pro model uses a sparse architecture that only activates 42 billion parameters during any single forward pass and has a Multi-Token Prediction layer that allows it to anticipate and generate multiple tokens simultaneously.
- China's promotion of OpenClaw is part of its vision for widespread AI integration by 2030, with the goal of making AI accessible to everyone, from "gearheads to grandmas".
- Anthropic's study found that people's desires for AI include professional excellence and life improvements, while their main concerns revolve around AI unreliability and job displacement.
- MiniMax's M2.7 model supports complex workflows in software engineering, office productivity, and research environments, and features capabilities like autonomous debugging and research agent harnesses.
- GPT 5.4 is a new model that brings improved usability and "agentness", making it feel like it can do a lot of random tasks, and is the first OpenAI agent that feels like it can do a lot of random tasks.
- Anthropic is leveraging its early-adopter base to go mainstream, with data suggesting that the company's tools are becoming the consumer default, but the company still struggles to meet its own demand.
- Stripe announced support for programmable LLMs, enabling businesses to create customized payment experiences, and Microsoft's Agent Package Manager is an open-source, community-driven dependency manager for AI agents.

newsletters.summary:
## The Code

### Key Highlights
- MiniMax M2.7, a new model from Chinese AI labs, rivals top models like OpenAI and Anthropic on coding benchmarks, demonstrating significant advancements in AI technology.
- The M2.7 model completed over 100 loops of autonomous self-improvement without human intervention, showcasing its capabilities in self-evolving AI.
- OpenAI released smaller models designed to bring GPT-5.4's power to latency-sensitive workloads, aiming to enhance coding efficiency.
- Anthropic introduced Dispatch, a new research preview within Claude Cowork, allowing for persistent conversations on desktops and enhancing workflow automation.

### Detailed Points
- MiniMax M2.7's performance on SWE-Pro and VIBE-Pro benchmarks highlights its potential in coding tasks, with scores comparable to top models like GPT-5.3-Codex.
- The model's ability to support native multi-agent collaboration and maintain high skill adherence across various tools underscores its versatility and reliability.
- OpenAI's smaller models, GPT-5.4 mini and GPT-5.4 nano, are designed for faster execution and lower latency, making them suitable for real-time applications and lightweight subtasks.
- Anthropic's Dispatch feature in Claude Cowork enables users to assign tasks and return to completed work later, streamlining workflow management and enhancing productivity.
- The concept of "harness engineering" emphasizes the importance of designing environments and feedback loops to make AI agents reliable and efficient, rather than solely focusing on model improvements.
- Examples from LangChain and Anthropic demonstrate how redesigning the harness can significantly improve agent performance, highlighting the potential for harness engineering in AI development.

### Key Highlights
- OpenAI has signed a deal with Amazon Web Services (AWS) to make its AI products available to the U.S. government for both classified and unclassified work.

- Microsoft is reorganizing its Copilot teams to unify the consumer and business experiences.

- NASA's X-43 jet, which reached speeds of 11,854 km/h, is an example of innovative technology that has contributed to advancements in various fields.

newsletters.subject: LIVE WEBINAR - Real Intent Launches Superagent at NAR '25
newsletters.summary:
## The Tech Buzz

### Key Highlights
- Real Intent is launching Superagent, a full-service growth automation platform for real estate agents and brokerages, at NAR '25.
- A live webinar is scheduled for March 19th at 1PM PST / 4PM EST to unveil Superagent and demonstrate its capabilities.
- Superagent aims to make agents "snap-finger famous" in their zipcode by automatically generating awareness, conversing with leads, and handing them off to agents.
- Real Intent's solution is claimed to be up to 90% more affordable than Zillow's Premier Agent service.

### Detailed Points
- Real Intent is a company that helps real estate professionals leverage advanced technologies to identify motivated sellers and buyers using intent data.
- The live webinar will cover how intent data can give agents a competitive edge in their market, and feature real-world examples of agents successfully leveraging intent data.
- Agents who have used Real Intent's program have seen significant results, including increased seller meetings and listings.
- Real Intent is currently only working with 1 broker or agent per zip code, making zip code availability exclusive.
- The webinar will also discuss how Real Intent's solution can be an effective and affordable alternative to Zillow's Premier Agent service.
- Real Intent's platform uses intent data to identify motivated sellers and buyers at the optimal time, and can automatically generate awareness and converse with leads.
- The company claims that its solution can help agents achieve more wins, fewer hours, and higher profits.
